findings.reason: the followup's name set is what a coordinator dispatches from.
findings.text: f-wftl-010 names §30, §37 and §39, each declared done in this same version (plan.html:219) and closed by its own comment, and its recommended invocation builds §39, while §40 and §41 — declared implementable at plan.html:221 and :225 and named by no other followup — appear in no followup at all, so a coordinator driving the plan from its only open followup dispatches three landed sections and never dispatches the two new ones

findings.reason: without the unstored case the section's central distinction between a review run's own record and a review of itself is unmeasured on the side where deleting it destroys evidence.
findings.text: §41's cases cover a review run whose record is stored and retired, one inside its window, and an implementation run whose review is owed and kept, but no case plants a review run past its window whose review record is not stored, so an implementation that ignores the record entirely and retires every review run past its window satisfies every case while contradicting the Deliverable's "its stored review record"

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §40's cited commits resolve (`11ae57aaee` is a two-parent merge repair with `6d4266db9b` an ancestor of it); §41's `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs`, `~/.cache/reckon-gpfs-footprint/retention-dry-1313428.log` (job 1313428), `reckon-crew-retention.timer` (reckon/crew/gc.py:1694), `--install-timer` and `--limit` (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2101-2125) all resolve, and the timer service's exec line is `python -m reckon.crew.gc --apply` as the Why states (reckon/crew/gc.py:2101).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §41's four done-when cases (plan.html:226) plant a review run whose review record is stored but never one whose record is not, so an implementation that retires every review run past its window regardless of its record passes every case.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections write their gate evidence to the plan's landed archive (docs/evidence/archive/work-flows-to-the-lane-landed.html resolves), and §41's cited dry-run log is a durable path under ~/.cache that exists and reads as described.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §40 and §41 name no ticket, plan label, version tag or changelog prose in their deliverables or write paths; their test names state the behaviour.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §40's root cause (scope judged against the run's original base after a merge-repair merge) is supported by the cited evidence and its repair is checkable against the twenty-file population; §41's root cause (a review-tier guard that no review run can ever clear) is confirmed by its own cited log, whose 209 withheld rows are all review-owed and whose withheld run ids are dominated by review runs with review_tier full; neither section prescribes a code path, step sequence or function.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §40 delivers one rule for what a landing judges, and §41 one rule for what retention judges a review run on, the timer's exec line being the mechanism by which that retention runs at all.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the plan's only open followup, f-wftl-010 (plan.html:284-286), names §30, §37 and §39, all declared done at plan.html:219 and closed by c-close-s30 and c-close-s39, and recommends `/reckon-build work-flows-to-the-lane §39`, while the two sections this version newly declares implementable, §40 and §41 (plan.html:221, :225), are named by no followup.
